prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs. To steer you to the right interior painter in St. Louis, tell me a few quick things and I’ll give specific recommendations:

Questions
- Is this a residential or commercial job?
- How many rooms / approximate square footage, and are there major repairs (drywall, trim, popcorn ceiling removal)?
- Desired timeline?
- Budget range or target price?
- Do you want color consultation, wallpaper removal, or specialty finishes?

If you’d like to decide yourself, here’s how to choose the best company and what to ask:

How to choose
- Reputation: Look for high ratings and recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, and Facebook. Prefer companies with many recent positive reviews, not just a few older ones.
- Local experience: A locally based crew will understand St. Louis climate issues (humidity, prep needs) and likely be easier to reach.
- Insurance & license: Ask for proof of liability insurance and worker’s comp. Licensed contractors are preferable.
- Written estimate & contract: Get itemized written bids that list prep, paint brand/finish, number of coats, surface repairs, timelines, cleanup, and warranty.
- References & portfolio: Ask for recent local references and photos of completed interiors similar to your project.
- Paint products & warranty: Reputable companies use quality paints (Sherwin-Williams, Benjamin Moore, etc.) and stand behind their work with a warranty.
- Communication & professionalism: Responsiveness, punctuality, and clear scope are strong signals.

Questions to ask each painter
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you have references from similar St. Louis interior jobs?
- What brand and sheen of paint will you use and why?
- How many coats will you apply? Do you include primer?
- Who does the prep work (patching, sanding, caulking)? Is that included?
- What’s your timeline and schedule for the job?
- What’s your payment schedule and cancellation policy?
- Do you offer a warranty or touch-up guarantee?

Red flags
- No written contract or estimate
- Requests for large cash upfront payments
- Very low bids markedly below others (may cut corners)
- Poor or no references, or many recent negative reviews

If you want, I can:
- Pull current top-rated interior painting companies in St. Louis and give you a short vetted list
- Prepare an email or checklist you can send to painters to get estimates

Which would you prefer?
